## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the proof check because it reports requirements with no criteria as proven and raises an exception when a criterion’s proof flag is null.

## Changes

The pull request changes how requirement proof is calculated and adds a batch helper that rejects empty batches and checks whether every entry has been reviewed. It adds tests for both helpers.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — Keep empty requirements unproven — `requirement_proven([])` returns `True` because both the sum and the number of criteria are zero. The previous implementation required at least one criterion. — Callers can report a requirement as proven even when it has no supporting criteria.
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — Preserve truth-value checks for proof flags — `requirement_proven([{"proven": None}])` raises `TypeError` because `sum` tries to add `None` to an integer. The previous predicate treated the null flag as false. — A criterion with a null proof flag prevents callers from getting the requirement’s proof status.
